transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janene Herbst.
With just weeks to go to the midterm elections that will determine control of Congress now in Republican hands,
President Trump is on a campaign rally swing in traditional Republican stronghold states.
Today he'll be in Ohio, where just days ago, 1,400 factory workers were laid off.
Voters have a lot to think about, including the economy and the Iran war.
NPR's Ron Elving has more.
Right now there's a lot of attention being paid to the seats the Democrats are targeting, including Trump states,
such as Texas, a recently Ohio, North Carolina, and Alaska, and even Kansas,
where no Democrat has won a Senate seat since 1932.
But I'm also watching the seats the Democrats need to defend if they want to take over the Senate.
The seats they have now in New Hampshire, Michigan, and Minnesota,
retirements have left them vulnerable in these states,
and holding on to what you have is essential if you want to make a takeover push in the Senate.
NPR's Ron Elving reporting.
It's not just gas prices that are high.
The average price of jet fuel hit a new high last month.
NPR's Joel Rose has more.
The average price for a gallon of jet fuel climbed to $4.37 in September,
according to the tracking firm Argus.
Airlines for America, the industry trade group that represents the major airlines,
says that sets a new all-time high, narrowly eclipsing the previous record set in April,
shortly after the war in Iran began.
The group says airlines are cutting flights and retiring older aircraft to keep costs down.
But carriers are also passing some of their fuel costs on to the consumer.
The average domestic airfare has reached its highest point of the year,
according to the travel website Kayak, at more than $400, with the holiday travel season looming.
Joel Rose, NPR News, Washington.
In Spain, protests are taking place across the country
a week after thousands took to the streets to demand urgent action by the government
to address a national housing crisis.
It all started with the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, as NPR's Miguel Macias reports.
Much has happened since the protests started a week ago.
After 87-year-old Maria del Carmen Gavascal was evicted from her rental apartment in Madrid.
The government of Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez drafted two emergency housing decrees in a rush
negotiating with these coalition members.
While all parties in Spain agree there is a national problem with the price of rental housing,
they did not agree on a solution.
On Friday, Sanchez's measures were voted down.
In Congress, there's been plenty of finger-pointing
and speculation that Sanchez might call snap elections for late November,
as he sees an opportunity to come from behind in the polls thanks to an energized left.
On the streets, protesters continue to demand solutions now.
Miguel Macias, NPR News, Seville, Spain.
This is NPR News.
RM, the K-pop idol and leader of the globe-trotting boy band BTS, has turned museum curator.
NPR's Globe Development reports a new exhibition opening today at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
is the first ever to feature the South Korean Superstars art collection.
The exhibition includes well over 100 works from RM's collection.
It highlights ancient and contemporary Korean paintings, objects and sculptures,
including works by some of RM's favorite artists, like Kim Won-ki and Yeon Hyong-kyun.
At a press briefing for the show, the self-deprecating musician said he loves collecting art,
but also feels guilty about it.
Do I really need to carry so many unnecessary things that I don't even need?
Have I ended up becoming just a boring, rich snore?
Well, maybe.
RM started collecting art in 2019.
He sings about his passion on tracks like Still Life.
Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
The Smithsonian Institution is using artificial intelligence
to try to better understand its American Revolution collections.
Officials say the project will help both the public and scholars
connect objects across institutions, including the Library of Congress.
The goal is to find new stories about people whose lives have faded from history.
The Smithsonian says it does understand the concerns about the use of AI,
but it emphasizes that they will be using human oversight.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: President Trump campaigns in Ohio weeks before midterm elections determining Congressional control
Democrats target Republican stronghold Senate seats in Texas, Ohio, North Carolina, Alaska, Kansas
Average jet fuel price hits record high of $4.37 per gallon in September
Airlines cut flights and retire older aircraft to manage rising fuel costs
Average domestic airfare reaches highest point of year at over $400
Spain protests continue after 87-year-old woman evicted, demanding government housing crisis action
Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's emergency housing decrees voted down in Congress
RM from BTS curates first exhibition of his art collection at San Francisco Museum
Exhibition features over 100 works including ancient and contemporary Korean paintings and sculptures
Smithsonian Institution uses artificial intelligence to better understand American Revolution collections
